A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same port-Hamiltonian DGN work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite title, terminology and layout changes.

before.justification: Sections 3.1-3.4 and Appendix D report original simulations, graph-transfer and graph-property experiments, peptide benchmark results and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds Hamiltonian baseline comparisons, memory measurements and Minesweeper and driving-force experiments.

M1.justification: The architecture and force families remain, with H-DGN renamed conservative PH-DGN/PH-DGNC. However, Appendix A.3 changes the Hamiltonian-gradient and external-force arguments from q^(ell+1) in v1 Eq. (13) to q^ell in v2 Eq. (14), revising the stated momentum update. This does not establish that implementations or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds the Minesweeper counting task. The Carbon-60 simulation, three graph-transfer topologies and distances, three graph-property tasks and two peptide tasks remain, making this a limited extension of coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds HamGNN and HANG to graph-property and runtime comparisons (Tables 1 and 4), and SWAN to LRGB comparisons (Tables 2 and 5). The new Minesweeper comparison also introduces SGFormer and Polynormer. These substantially extend the evaluated competitors, especially the directly relevant Hamiltonian methods previously only discussed.

E3.justification: Existing core splits, training budgets and Table 3 grids remain. New evaluations introduce Minesweeper ROC-AUC with two-stage selection of a conservative configuration followed by force ablations, Hamiltonian-baseline search settings and memory measurement, and GCNII under the modified LRGB protocol. These extend the protocols without replacing the main evaluation design.

E4.justification: V1 already compared conservative and full models on graph properties and peptides. V2 Appendix D.4 adds a systematic Minesweeper ablation of damping/external-force combinations and a conservative-versus-driven comparison on all three graph-transfer topologies (Figure 5), substantially expanding analysis of when the components help.

E5.justification: Table 8 newly reports averages and variability over ten official train/validation/test splits for Minesweeper. Retained graph-transfer/property experiments and runtimes still use four initializations, and peptides three; no increase in their run counts or new significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: Retained proposed-model scores are unchanged, but v2 adds baseline scores, memory measurements, driven transfer curves and Minesweeper results, including PH-DGNC test ROC-AUC 98.45 +/- 0.21. Table 2 replaces GCNII AP/MAE 0.5543/0.3471 with 0.6444/0.2507 under the modified protocol; Table 5 retains the original-setting results, so this is not a same-setting gain.

T1.justification: V2 adds Theorem 2.4 and its Appendix B.6 proof on cross-node sensitivity, plus three Appendix B.7 theorems bounding one-step sensitivity with driving forces under boundedness and Lipschitz assumptions. This substantially extends v1's conservative-system energy and sensitivity analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a general port-Hamiltonian framework, conservative information-preservation guarantees, configurable aggregation and forces, and strong long-range performance. The explicit first-port-Hamiltonian claim in v2's introduction already appeared in v1's related work.

C2.justification: V2 adds task-dependent guidance on driving forces, hypothesizes adaptive noise filtering on peptides, and interprets the new sensitivity bound as supporting propagation. It removes Appendix E's explicit discussion of the computation-accuracy trade-off and possible superiority of transformers/rewiring. Gradient-growth cautions remain in Section 3.1 and Appendix A.1.

D1.justification: Section 3 supplies a concrete code-repository pointer instead of only promising release upon acceptance, although the new reproducibility statement retains that promise. V2 also specifies graph-transfer target construction, baseline implementation sources and new experiment grids. These are documentation/access additions; existing core hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Section 4 and new Appendix D.3/Table 6 substantially expand positioning against the already-cited HamGNN and HANG, distinguishing explicit message passing, graph coupling and learnable driving forces. V2 also adds literature on temporal DGNs, SWAN, adaptive propagation and the Minesweeper evaluation.

P1.justification: V2 revises the title and author information, unifies terminology around PH-DGN and PH-DGNC, expands selected explanations, and adds ethics, reproducibility and acknowledgment sections. The main section order and much existing prose remain; most additional length comes from new scientific material.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 6-8 and Figure 5, expands comparison tables, and reorganizes LRGB displays with source/protocol groups and PE/SE labels. Table 7 repeats accuracy/runtime entries from Tables 1 and 4 alongside new memory figures, while Figure 5 extends the retained transfer plot. The document also adopts ICLR typography and headers.

improvement.justification: Direct Hamiltonian comparisons, memory measurements and the driving-force ablations in Appendices D.3-D.4 strengthen validation and reveal when the conservative variant is preferable. Explicit transfer targets and a code pointer improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removal of substantive limitations and by interpreting a looser sensitivity upper bound as support for propagation without establishing stronger sensitivity, limiting the overall improvement.
